title: Bug:snappi: traffic_generation.py: dut_port_config is used as both list and dict.
author: rraghav-cisco
body:

### Importance or Severity

### Description of the bug

comments.author: yxieca
comments.body:
**AI review — Changes requested**

### Blocking

- tests/common/snappi_tests/traffic_generation.py (function multi_base_traffic_config, initialization at the changed lines; and the returned base_flow_config["dut_port_config"]): This is a public-contract change on the returned value shape (list-of-two-dicts -> {"Tx": [...], "Rx": [...]}). Within this file the new shape is already what other code expects — setup_base_traffic_config() constructs the exact same dict form, generate_test_flows() iterates dut_port_config["Tx"] / dut_port_config["Rx"], and run_traffic() reads base_flow_config["dut_port_config"]["Tx"][0].values() — so the fix is internally consistent. However, multi_base_traffic_config()'s return value is consumed by callers outside this file (tests under tests/snappi_tests/... and related helpers referenced by issue #22197), and the diff does not include or cite a grep of those callers. Please either (a) include in this PR (or link in the description) the specific caller sites that consume the returned dut_port_config — confirming none still index it positionally as dut_port_config[0] / dut_port_config[1] — or (b) add a small assertion/unit test that locks the {"Tx","Rx"} contract so any positional-access regression fails fast. Without that, end-to-end shape consistency for external consumers cannot be confirmed from the diff.

### Grounded nits

- tests/common/snappi_tests/traffic_generation.py (updated docstring in multi_base_traffic_config): The new example {"Tx": [{'Ethernet4':[3, 4]}], "Rx": [{'Ethernet8':[3, 4]}]} matches the new initialization (each list gets exactly one appended dict). Consider a one-line note that each of "Tx"/"Rx" currently holds a single peer-port dict here, while the sibling setup_base_traffic_config() documents/produces the multi-port form ({"Tx": [{'Ethernet4':[3,4]}, {'Ethernet12':[3,4]}], "Rx": [{'Ethernet8':[3,4]}]}), so readers don't assume the two functions differ in contract.
- tests/common/snappi_tests/traffic_generation.py (tx_dict / rx_dict locals at the changed lines): Names remain clear and intent-preserving; change is minimal and localized — no action needed.

comments.author: MahekPatel-2403
comments.body:
Thanks for the review.

I audited all consumers of multi_base_traffic_config() to verify the contract change.

Specifically, I inspected:

-tests/snappi_tests/pfcwd/files/pfcwd_actions_helper.py
-tests/snappi_tests/pfc/files/pfc_congestion_helper.py
-tests/snappi_tests/pfc/files/mixed_speed_multidut_helper.py

All three callers simply append the returned base_flow_config to snappi_extra_params.base_flow_config_list and do not access dut_port_config directly.

I also searched the codebase for any remaining positional accesses (dut_port_config[0] / dut_port_config[1]) and found none. All current accesses use the dictionary-based contract (dut_port_config["Tx"] / dut_port_config["Rx"]). Existing expressions such as dut_port_config["Tx"][0] index into the list stored under the "Tx" key and are consistent with the updated structure.

I also updated the multi_base_traffic_config() docstring to clarify that this helper currently creates a single port-mapping dictionary per direction, while setup_base_traffic_config() may produce multiple port-mapping dictionaries per direction, with both helpers following the same {"Tx", "Rx"} contract.
